about: Plain-English healthcare form terms. Every explanation the app gives is grounded in these definitions. A teacher should review each entry and set vetted to true. Translations added under translations.<language code> are treated as teacher-approved and are shown word for word instead of a computer translation.

terms.definition: A set amount of money you pay each time you see a doctor or pick up a medicine.
terms.example: My copay for each doctor visit is $20.

terms.definition: The amount you must pay for care each year before your insurance starts to help pay.
terms.example: My deductible is $1,000, so I pay the first $1,000 of my care this year.

terms.definition: The part of a bill you share with your insurance, shown as a percent, like 20%.
terms.example: My coinsurance is 20%, so I pay $20 when the bill is $100.

terms.definition: The money you pay every month to keep your health insurance.
terms.example: My insurance premium is $150 every month.

terms.definition: The most money you will have to pay for covered care in one year.
terms.example: After I reach my out-of-pocket maximum, my insurance pays for the rest of my covered care this year.

terms.definition: A card from your health plan that shows your name and your plan numbers.
terms.example: Please show your insurance card at the front desk.

terms.definition: The number on your insurance card that shows who you are to your health plan.
terms.example: Write the member ID from the front of your card.

terms.definition: The number on your insurance card for your plan, often the plan from your job.
terms.example: The group number is under my name on the card.

terms.definition: The person whose name the health insurance plan is under.
terms.example: My husband is the policyholder because the insurance comes from his job.

terms.definition: Your main health plan, the one that pays first.
terms.example: My primary insurance is from my job, so they pay first.

terms.definition: A second health plan that can help pay what your first plan does not pay.
terms.example: I have secondary insurance through my wife's job.

terms.definition: Doctors and hospitals that have a deal with your insurance, so care costs you less.
terms.example: This clinic is in-network, so my visit costs less.

terms.definition: Doctors and hospitals that do not have a deal with your insurance, so care often costs more.
terms.example: That hospital is out-of-network, so I might get a bigger bill.

terms.definition: A bill that is sent to your insurance company to ask them to pay for your care.
terms.example: The clinic sent a claim to my insurance after my visit.

terms.definition: A paper from your insurance that shows what they paid and what you may owe; it is not a bill.
terms.example: My Explanation of Benefits says my insurance paid $80 for my visit.

terms.definition: Permission your insurance must give before you get some tests, medicines, or treatments.
terms.example: My MRI needs prior authorization from my insurance first.

terms.definition: A note from your main doctor that sends you to see a different, special doctor.
terms.example: I need a referral to see a heart doctor.

terms.definition: California's free or low-cost health insurance for people with low income.
terms.example: My children have Medi-Cal, so their visits do not cost money.

terms.definition: Health insurance from the U.S. government for people 65 or older and some people with disabilities.
terms.example: My grandmother uses Medicare to pay for her doctor visits.

terms.definition: The money you still need to pay on a bill.
terms.example: The balance due on my bill is $35.

terms.definition: The person who agrees to pay the bill, like a parent paying for a child.
terms.example: I am the guarantor for my son's doctor bills.

terms.definition: Paying for care with your own money, without using insurance.
terms.example: I do not have insurance, so I am self-pay.

terms.definition: An agreement that you will pay any part of the bill your insurance does not pay.
terms.example: I signed the financial responsibility form at the front desk.

terms.definition: Permission for your insurance to send payment straight to the doctor's office instead of to you.
terms.example: The assignment of benefits lets my insurance pay the clinic directly.

terms.definition: Your main doctor, who you see for checkups and common health problems.
terms.example: My primary care provider is Dr. Lee.

terms.definition: A doctor who knows a lot about one part of the body or one kind of illness.
terms.example: My doctor sent me to a specialist for my skin.

terms.definition: A clinic for problems that need care today but are not life-threatening, like a bad cold or a small cut.
terms.example: I went to urgent care for my hurt ankle.

terms.definition: The hospital area for very serious problems, like chest pain or trouble breathing.
terms.example: Go to the emergency room or call 911 if you have chest pain.

terms.definition: A set day and time to see a doctor or nurse.
terms.example: My appointment is on Monday at 9:00 a.m.

terms.definition: Telling the front desk you have arrived and giving them your information.
terms.example: Please come 15 minutes early for check-in.

terms.definition: Another visit after your first one, so the doctor can check how you are doing.
terms.example: The doctor wants a follow-up visit in two weeks.

terms.definition: A visit once a year to check your health, even when you are not sick.
terms.example: I get my annual physical every January.

terms.definition: Seeing a doctor by video or phone instead of going to the office.
terms.example: I had a telehealth visit on my phone.

terms.definition: A person who helps you talk with the doctor in your language, usually for free.
terms.example: I asked for an interpreter for my appointment.

terms.definition: The rules about what happens, like a fee, if you miss a visit or cancel too late.
terms.example: The cancellation policy says to call one day before if you cannot come.

terms.definition: The main health problem or need that brought you to the doctor today.
terms.example: My reason for visit is a cough that will not go away.

terms.definition: Someone who has never seen this doctor or clinic before.
terms.example: I filled out a new patient form at my first visit.

terms.definition: A website or app where you can see test results, send messages to your doctor, and make visits.
terms.example: I can see my test results on the patient portal.

terms.definition: A check of your blood, urine, or other samples to learn about your health.
terms.example: The doctor ordered a lab test to check my blood sugar.

terms.definition: The day, month, and year you were born.
terms.example: Write your date of birth like this: 03/15/1985.

terms.definition: The street, city, and ZIP code where you get your mail.
terms.example: Write your mailing address so the clinic can send you letters.

terms.definition: A person the clinic can call if something serious happens to you.
terms.example: I put my sister as my emergency contact.

terms.definition: How a person is connected to you, like mother, husband, or friend.
terms.example: Next to relationship to patient, I wrote daughter.

terms.definition: Your name written by hand in your own way to show you agree.
terms.example: Put your signature at the bottom of the page.

terms.definition: An adult who has the legal right to make decisions for a child or another person.
terms.example: A parent or legal guardian must sign for children under 18.

terms.definition: The language you want to use when you talk with the doctor and read papers.
terms.example: I wrote my preferred language on the form so they can call an interpreter.

terms.definition: Whether you are single, married, divorced, or widowed.
terms.example: For marital status, I checked married.

terms.definition: Something you write when a question is not about you or your situation.
terms.example: I do not have a second insurance, so I wrote N/A.

terms.definition: The number the clinic uses to find your health file.
terms.example: The clinic uses my medical record number to find my file.

terms.definition: Foods, medicines, plants, or other things that make your body react badly, like a rash or swelling.
terms.example: I have allergies to peanuts and penicillin.

terms.definition: Information about your past illnesses, health problems, and treatments.
terms.example: The doctor asked about my medical history.

terms.definition: Health problems that your parents, brothers, sisters, or grandparents have had.
terms.example: Diabetes is in my family history because my mother has it.

terms.definition: Changes in your body that show you may be sick, like fever, pain, or cough.
terms.example: My symptoms are a sore throat and a fever.

terms.definition: The name the doctor gives to your illness or health problem after checking you.
terms.example: The diagnosis was an ear infection.

terms.definition: A health problem that lasts a long time, like diabetes or high blood pressure.
terms.example: High blood pressure is a chronic condition.

terms.definition: Treatment where a doctor opens part of your body to fix a problem, usually in a hospital.
terms.example: I had surgery on my knee in 2019.

terms.definition: Medicine, usually given with a needle, that protects you from certain diseases, like the flu.
terms.example: My son needs his immunizations before school starts.

terms.definition: Whether you smoke cigarettes, vape, or use chewing products.
terms.example: The form asks about tobacco use, so I checked never.

terms.definition: All the medicines, vitamins, and pills you take now.
terms.example: Bring a list of your current medications to every visit.

terms.definition: A doctor's written order for a medicine you can only get from a pharmacy.
terms.example: The doctor sent my prescription to the pharmacy.

terms.definition: How much medicine to take and how often to take it.
terms.example: The dosage is one pill two times a day.

terms.definition: Getting more of the same medicine after you finish it.
terms.example: I called the pharmacy for a refill.

terms.definition: A store where you pick up your medicine.
terms.example: My pharmacy is the one near my house.

terms.definition: A cheaper medicine that works the same as the brand-name one.
terms.example: The generic drug costs $4 instead of $40.

terms.definition: An unwanted change in your body from a medicine, like feeling sleepy or sick.
terms.example: One side effect of this medicine is a dry mouth.

terms.definition: Medicine you can buy at a store without a doctor's note, like many pain pills.
terms.example: I take an over-the-counter medicine for headaches.

terms.definition: Vitamins, herbs, or other products you take to stay healthy that are not medicine from a doctor.
terms.example: Please list any supplements you take, like fish oil.

terms.definition: Saying yes, usually by signing, that you agree to a treatment or test.
terms.example: I signed a consent form before my blood test.

terms.definition: A paper that explains how the clinic keeps your health information private and who can see it.
terms.example: The front desk gave me a Notice of Privacy Practices to read.

aliases: authorization for release of health information
terms.definition: Your permission for the clinic to share your health records with another person or office.
terms.example: I signed a release of information so my new doctor can see my records.

terms.definition: A paper that says what care you want, and who will decide for you, if you become too sick to speak.
terms.example: The hospital asked if I have an advance directive.
